blocks.name: Block 1 · Foundation
blocks.tag: Block 1 of 6 · v12 · Road to Font

weeks.label: Establish
weeks.focus: First week on the platform: empty bar → light on the Olympic lifts, squat/deadlift/RDL at RPE 6. Board A: 12–15 attempts at V5–V6 plus one V7 project. Take the four mobility baselines and start the daily stretch. Weigh every morning; weigh and photograph everything you eat for the first three days to find where the calories live.

weeks.label: Build
weeks.focus: Small load adds only where every rep was snappy. Board A: 12–15 attempts, same grades. Repeaters to 4 sets. Birthday week — a milestone, not a peak; dinner out is fine, the no-alcohol line holds.

weeks.label: Peak
weeks.focus: Board A: 15–18 attempts, V6 projects plus the V7. Olympic lifts from the hang at working loads, RPE 7 cap. Repeaters 5 sets. Hardest week of the block.

weeks.label: Deload + test
weeks.focus: Board sessions halved at V4–V5. Barbell ~60%, one fewer set. Repeaters 2 easy sets. Maintenance calories all week. Retest the four baselines and do the first 7-s max-hang load test on Saturday.

blocks.intro: Block 1 of six on the road to Fontainebleau in April. Starts Mon Oct 26, runs through Sun Nov 22. The platform is done, so this is the first block with everything in it: board Monday and Thursday, hangboard repeaters and the barbell Wednesday and Saturday, easy runs with the stretching block Tuesday, Friday and Sunday. Reliable V4–V5 and a V7 best is the starting line; this block trains at V5–V6 with one V7 project and builds the tissue tolerance the next five blocks spend. Olympic lifts are the centerpiece of the lifting because you love them and because power is what a 40° board wants. Muscle and neural strength return in weeks after a layoff; tendons, pulleys and discs take months — RPE 7 is the ceiling all month. The deficit is biggest this block because the board is easiest; the scale target is ~191 by Nov 22. No alcohol for the 26 weeks — the old three-a-night was the whole deficit and most of the lost sleep. The full 26-week plan lives in the Road to Fontainebleau doc.
rules: RPE 7 is the ceiling this month. No 8s exist. Crisp reps only.
Olympic lifts are governed by bar speed, not load. Add weight only after three consecutive sessions where every rep was snappy — no press-outs, no slow catches.
Board attempts are counted. 12–15 quality attempts is a session; sloppy attempts end it. Full crimp stays off limit attempts.

No alcohol, through April. Three drinks a night was 400–700 kcal — the whole deficit — and the reason sleep never fully recovered. Sparkling water or an NA beer with dinner; the first week of sleep is rougher, then it gets better than it has been in years.
No power-endurance this block. It enters in Block 2 as 3×3.
Four finger days a week is the ceiling. If Thursday fingers feel heavy, Wednesday's hangs were too much — cut them next week before touching the board.
Hangboard days are conditioning, not training. If a repeater session feels like work, it was too heavy.
The run is the first thing dropped when fatigue stacks. The stretching block is never dropped.
recovery: Eating pattern: black coffee before training, then three meals — breakfast within an hour of finishing (or 60–90 min before if training late morning), lunch ~12:30, family dinner. Block 1 deficit is 500–600 kcal: training days 2,400–2,600 kcal; run/rest days 2,200–2,400. Week 4 (deload) at maintenance, ~2,900–3,100. Target 0.75–1 lb/week; ~191 lb by Nov 22.

Alcohol: none for the 26 weeks (decided Oct 22). Expect a quick 2–4 lb drop in the first ten days that is water and glycogen, not fat. If the 7-day average then falls faster than 1.25 lb/week, add 200 kcal back at lunch — removing the drinks and running the food deficit together can overshoot.
Protein 165–190 g/day as three doses of 55–65 g, 4–6 hours apart — higher in a deficit, not lower. Breakfast 55–60 g, lunch 55–65 g, dinner 55–65 g.

Where the deficit lives: lunch starch and fat. Never the protein, never dinner's social side. Weigh daily, judge the 7-day average; flat two weeks → 200 off lunch; falling faster than 1.25 lb/week → 200 back on.

Creatine 5 g monohydrate daily including rest days, in the morning water. Vitamin D 2,000 IU D3 with lunch. Optional: collagen 15 g + vitamin C 45 min before hang days — mixed evidence, cheap, plausible for 50-year-old pulleys.
Water: ~3 L on training days, ~2.5 L on rest days, coffee included. Pale-straw urine by mid-morning; post-training weight within 1 lb of pre. A pinch of salt in the morning water.
Sleep 7.5+ hours; caffeine cutoff ~1 pm. A deficit makes sleep matter more, not less.
Deficit tripwire: bar speed dying across sets two sessions running, or two flat board sessions in a row → eat 300 more at lunch for a week and cut the Sunday run before anything else.

Warning signs that outrank the plan: sharp finger pain, pulley tenderness the morning after, medial elbow ache, overhead shoulder pinch, hamstring grab under the sit-bone, or low-back tightness past a day → drop that movement, keep easy volume, note it in the app.
tests: Active straight-leg raise: doorway, mark where the heel lands
90/90 sit: both sit-bones down, hands off the floor? which side is worse
Board heel height: highest hold you can place a heel on, hips open, both hands on
Core baselines: hollow hold time, hanging knee raises, tuck L-sit, tuck front lever
Week 4 only: 7-s max hang load on 20 mm half-crimp (bodyweight + X) — sets Block 2's max-hang loads

run_rest.label: Easy run or rest
run_rest.note: Sunday's run is the first thing to drop if fatigue stacks. Keep the flexibility block either way.

tb2a.title: TB2 Session A
tb2a.subtitle: Monday limit · V5–V6 projects + one V7

items.name: RowErg
items.detail: 5 min easy.

items.name: Shoulders, wrists, fingers
items.detail: Band pull-aparts ×15, arm and wrist circles, finger pumps (tendon glides), gentle flexor and extensor stretches. Band pull-aparts: youtu.be/Xg58d9lDWME · full 10-min warm-up: youtu.be/T_-kvmqCzbs

items.name: Dynamic hips (~4 min)
items.detail: Leg swings both planes ×10/leg · goblet squat pry 60 s · hip CARs ×5/side · active heel lifts toward hip height ×6/side. Dynamic only — no long static holds before hard climbing. Goblet pry: youtu.be/aEbQO49ru4Q · hip CARs: youtu.be/zbH4XmSREoc

items.name: On the board
items.detail: 3–4 easy jug problems (V0–V1), then a V2 → V3 → V4 mini-pyramid. Open-hand first. Movement reference (deadpointing): linked.

byWeek.1: 12–15 quality attempts: 3–4 projects at V5–V6, 2–4 attempts each, 3–5 min rest. Up to 3 attempts on one V7 if fingers feel good. Half crimp / open hand only.
byWeek.2: 12–15 attempts at V5–V6 plus the V7 project. Same rests. Count attempts in the note.
byWeek.3: 15–18 attempts: V6 projects plus the V7. 3–5 min rest between attempts. This is the hardest board week of the block.
byWeek.4: 6–8 problems at V4–V5. Half session, deload.

items.name: Stop rule
items.detail: End the session when attempts get sloppy. The last 20% of a board session is where fingers get bought and sold.

items.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
items.detail: Knee on the crash pad, back foot flat on the floor (not up the wall), front foot well forward. Tuck the tailbone, squeeze the back glute, shift forward an inch. Weight stays on the back knee. The couch stretch's regression until this feels easy.

items.name: Daily target
items.detail: Block 1: 2,400–2,600 kcal · 165–190 g protein in three meals of 55–65 g. Estimated maintenance 2,900–3,200; this is a 500–600 kcal deficit — the biggest of the six blocks, because the board is easiest now. Week 4 at maintenance. Weigh daily, judge the 7-day average; target ~191 by Nov 22.

items.name: Before training
items.detail: Black coffee. 16 oz water with a pinch of salt (6,100 ft) and 5 g creatine. Fasted is fine under the RPE 7 cap — breakfast comes after. If you train later in the morning, eat breakfast 60–90 min before instead and keep it to the lighter version (yogurt + fruit, ~350 kcal).

items.name: Water
items.detail: ~3 L (100 oz) of fluids on training days; coffee counts. Front-load it: 16 oz on waking, 16 oz during the session, a glass with each meal covers most of it. Check: pale-straw urine by mid-morning, and body weight after training within 1 lb of before — each lb down is 16 oz to replace. Not a performance booster beyond that; it is the floor for a 195 lb man at 6,100 ft, where dry air and altitude diuresis push losses up. Do not force water past clear urine.

items.name: Breakfast (within 60 min after)
items.detail: 500–600 kcal · 55–60 g protein. Fast and repeatable: 3 eggs + 1 cup Greek yogurt + fruit, or a whey shake with milk + oats + banana. This replaces the old post-workout shake — it is the recovery feed and the first protein dose.

items.name: Lunch (~12:30–1:00) — the lever
items.detail: 800–950 kcal · 55–65 g protein first (7–8 oz lean meat/fish). Vegetables. Starch sized to the morning: a fist of rice/potato on board + lift days, half that on hang-only days. This is where the deficit lives — cut starch and fat here, never the protein. D3 2,000 IU with it.

items.name: Family dinner
items.detail: 1,000–1,200 kcal · 55–65 g protein first, whatever is served; carbs by feel; no seconds. Dinner stays social — the plan does not touch it beyond the protein rule. Breakfast covering a full dose means dinner no longer has to carry the day.

items.name: Caffeine cutoff
items.detail: Nothing caffeinated after ~1 pm. The 7.5-hour sleep rule is the real recovery supplement, and it matters more in a deficit.

items.name: Alcohol
items.detail: None, through April. The old three-a-night was 400–700 kcal and fragmented the second half of every night's sleep. NA IPA or sparkling water with dinner. Rough sleep for the first week is the rebound, not a reason to stop.

blocks.title: Low-grip pressing, hamstrings, and the core foundations

items.name: Push press
items.detail: The jerk's drive pattern. Crisp dip-drive, no grinding lockouts.

items.name: Ring dips
items.detail: Tempo 3-1-3 if easy. If you have a bench, bench press 3×5 can rotate in here — floor press off the platform works solo.

items.name: Turkish get-up
items.detail: Shoulder integrity under load. Slow, every position owned. 16–20 kg is plenty this block.

items.name: Ring hamstring curls
items.detail: 3–4 s eccentric. The heel-hook engine — knee flexion under load.

items.name: Hanging knee raises
items.detail: Start at your honest max-minus-one. Slow, no swing.

items.name: Tuck L-sit, feet assisting
items.detail: Hands on two heavy kettlebell handles as parallettes; shoulders pressed down away from the ears.

items.name: Reverse wrist curls + light curls
items.detail: Tendon care — the deliberate high-rep exception, always.

items.name: Band face pulls
items.detail: Band at eye level on the rack, elbows high and wide. Posture insurance for a board climber.

items.name: Pace
items.detail: Genuinely conversational at 6,100 ft — full sentences, not gasped fragments. Aerobic base, recovery circulation, and the delivery vehicle for the flexibility block.

items.name: Strides
items.detail: 4–6 × 15 s only after Friday or Sunday runs. Never before a board morning.

items.name: Daily target
items.detail: Block 1: 2,200–2,400 kcal · 165–190 g protein in three meals. Lower than training days by about the size of the lunch starch; same three protein doses. Week 4 at maintenance.

items.name: Before
items.detail: Fasted is fine for conversational running. Water with a pinch of salt; creatine in it as usual — creatine is daily, rest days included.

items.name: Water
items.detail: ~2.5 L (85 oz) of fluids; coffee counts. Same checks: pale-straw urine, glass with each meal. Thirst is a reliable guide on easy days — the target exists because a dry climate blunts it.

items.name: Meals
items.detail: Breakfast after the run, 500–600 kcal, 55–60 g protein. Lunch ~12:30, 55–65 g protein, vegetables, small or no starch. Dinner: protein first, 55–65 g, no seconds. Three doses of 55–65 g spaced 4–6 hours apart is the distribution the muscle-protein literature actually favors.

items.name: Fish
items.detail: Keep the two fish dinners a week; salmon, trout, or sardines cover omega-3 without a capsule.

items.name: Alcohol
items.detail: None. Rest days are where the habit used to live; sparkling water with dinner, and the sleep that follows is the recovery.

flex.title: Flexibility block
flex.subtitle: After the run · the heel-hook plan

items.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
items.detail: The couch stretch with the quad taken out: knee on the crash pad, back foot flat on the floor, front foot well forward. Tuck the tailbone, squeeze the back glute, then shift forward an inch — the stretch is in the front of the back hip, not the knee. Progression: back foot on a low box (week 3+), then shin up the wall when the box version is easy. Week 1: 30 s. Week 2: 45 s.

items.name: 90/90 + switches
items.detail: Sit tall, then chest over the front shin. Switch sides without hands — that switch is the heel-hook hip in motion.

items.name: Frog
items.detail: Knees wide, feet turned out, forearms down. Rock back toward the heels. The knee-out, toe-out position itself.

items.name: Elephant walks
items.detail: Hands on the floor or a box, straighten one leg and push the heel down while the other knee bends. Slow.

items.name: PNF hamstring (partner or strap)
items.detail: On your back, leg up, partner holds. Push into their hands 5 s at half effort, breathe out, relax, they take the leg higher. The one stretch that needs a second person.

items.name: Pigeon
items.detail: Front shin across the mat, back leg straight. Square the hips, fold forward. The closest floor shape to a high heel hook.

items.name: Hip flexor stretch + 90/90
items.detail: The two that matter most. Half-kneeling hip flexor (back foot on the floor) and 90/90 — stretches only, no curls. Same on any weekday you are wiped.

items.name: Never deloads
items.detail: 6/10 effort: a clear pull, no shaking, you can talk. Sharp front-of-hip pinch or pain behind the knee ends that stretch for the day.

hang.title: Hangboard repeaters
hang.subtitle: Tendon conditioning · end of warm-up, before the barbell

items.name: Grip / edge
items.detail: Half-crimp on a 20 mm or larger edge — start on the largest comfortable one.

items.name: Structure
items.detail: 7 s on / 3 s off × 6 reps = one set (~1 min). Rest 2–3 min between sets.

items.name: Intensity
items.detail: Feet assisting on a box, effort ≤5/10 on every set. You should finish feeling like you did almost nothing — that is the point.

items.name: Progression
items.detail: Reduce foot assistance only after a full session at ≤5/10 with zero next-day soreness. No added weight this block.

items.name: Form
items.detail: Scaps set, elbows soft, no shrugging into the ears. End any set where engagement degrades.

blocks.title: Two rules that keep this safe

items.name: Too heavy?
items.detail: If a session ever feels like training, it was too heavy — back the next one off.

items.name: Sore next morning?
items.detail: Finger or pulley soreness that survives the night → skip the next hang session entirely, no negotiation.

items.name: Equipment
items.detail: If the wall-mounted board isn't up yet, a portable hangboard slung over the SML-2C pull-up bar works today.

liftb.title: Lift B · Snatch day
liftb.subtitle: Fresh legs · straps on everything to spare the forearms for Thursday

items.name: Empty-bar overhead squat
items.detail: Assessment and mobility in one. Expect it to feel awful in Week 1 and noticeably better by Week 4.

items.name: Power snatch
items.detail: Every rep snappy. A press-out means the weight stays put. Hang variation (weeks 1–2): youtu.be/SpDPcj0W3Yw

byWeek.1: From the hang (above knee), empty bar → light, straps fine. 6×2.
byWeek.2: From the hang. Small load add only if every rep was snappy last week. 6×2.

items.name: Snatch balance or overhead squat
items.detail: Loaded shoulder, hip, and ankle mobility disguised as a lift.

items.name: Back squat
items.detail: The strength anchor, ramped gently.

items.name: Romanian deadlift — straps
items.detail: 3-second lowering to your deepest flat-back range. Loaded hamstring flexibility.

items.name: Rear-foot-elevated split squat
items.detail: Back foot on a box or the bench, front shin vertical. Single-leg strength and the hip-flexor length a high step needs.

items.name: Kettlebell swings
items.detail: Hips snap, arms relax, bell floats to chest height. Hinge power without grip cost — hook the handle loosely.

items.name: Hollow hold + side plank
items.detail: The hollow is the foundation under both the L-sit and the front lever. Side plank: youtu.be/JFBx8cpLRTw

items.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
items.detail: Knee on the crash pad, back foot flat on the floor (not up the wall), front foot well forward. Tuck the tailbone, squeeze the back glute, shift forward an inch. Weight stays on the back knee. The couch stretch's regression until this feels easy.

items.name: Same as Monday
items.detail: RowErg 5 min · shoulders/wrists/fingers · dynamic hip block · V0–V1 jugs then V2 → V3 → V4 mini-pyramid.

items.name: Pyramid
items.detail: Rest 2–3 min between problems. Precise feet, hip turn-in, breathing.

items.name: Two or three heel-hook problems
items.detail: Problems at V3–V5 that need a heel hook. Climbing, not a drill — the only point is that the hip range the stretching is buying gets used on the wall each week.

items.name: No power-endurance this block
items.detail: PE enters in Block 2 as 3×3.

liftc.title: Lift C · Clean & jerk day
liftc.subtitle: Grip, pull, and power · farthest from both board sessions

items.name: Front-rack stretch
items.detail: Elbows up, bar in the fingertips.

items.name: Empty-bar jerk drill
items.detail: Dip, drive, punch under. Groove the split (or power) jerk before load goes on.

items.name: Power clean + jerk
items.detail: Fast elbows, no forward press-out on the jerk. No straps on cleans. Hang variation (weeks 1–2): youtu.be/efHjodEVf9w · jerk: see warm-up drill.

byWeek.1: From the hang, empty bar → light. 6×(2+1).
byWeek.2: From the hang. Small add only if every rep was crisp. 6×(2+1).

items.name: Deadlift
items.detail: You keep your deadlift — moderate this month, crisp always.

items.name: Pull-up lock-off ladder
items.detail: Lock-off work concentrates stress on the medial elbow. If the inner elbow so much as whispers, drop this first. Medial elbow pain explainer: youtu.be/BrQOX6D4HF0

byWeek.1: 4×4–6 strict bodyweight with a 2 s top hold on every rep
byWeek.2: 5×4–6 strict bodyweight with a 2 s top hold
byWeek.3: 3×3 with a 5 s hold at 90° per rep (frenchie-lite) — or light weighted 4×3–5

items.name: Tuck front lever
items.detail: Rings or bar. Scaps depressed, hips at hand height, knees tucked tight.

byWeek.3: 4 sets, or open the tuck slightly

items.name: KB snatch + suitcase carry
items.detail: KB snatch first, then a heavy single-bell suitcase carry — resist the lean, hips level. Farmer carry: youtu.be/G-_FYQfur9w · suitcase: youtu.be/SXf6ePnQMJ8

items.name: Ring YTWs
items.detail: Shoulder care.
